Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
26-year-old woman with a 3-day history of worsening right-sided, photophobic headache suggestive of migraine.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Generalized headache worst around right eye, onset 3 days ago, constant with episodic surges; severity up to 8/10; dull → occasionally sharp; gradually worsening.  
• Associated symptoms: Photophobia (“hurts to look at bright lights”); visual flashes (“shooting lights”); nausea without vomiting; difficulty concentrating. No blurry vision, no focal weakness, no speech difficulty, no fever, no rash, no recent head injury. Neck pain/stiffness initially acknowledged then denied (conflict noted).  
• Past medical history: None reported. No prior diagnosed migraines.  
• Family history: Mother and sister with recurrent migraines.  
• Medications: None regularly. Self-treated with ibuprofen (three tablets/day; exact dose/strength not documented) with minimal relief.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Social / preventive: Works in IT, prolonged screen time; wears longstanding prescription glasses, no recent eye exam. Lives with 3 housemates. Social smoker and social alcohol use. Mild work stress.

Examination:
(No physical examination or vitals documented.)

Impression:
Probable migraine-type headache.

Plan:
• Provide stronger analgesia: options discussed – ensure adequate ibuprofen dosing (up to 2 tablets three times daily), prescribe naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented) +/- paracetamol or codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Advise keeping a headache diary to identify triggers.  
• Follow-up in 1–2 weeks; earlier if worsening headache, visual changes, limb weakness, or other concerning symptoms.  
• Consider prophylactic migraine therapy at follow-up if headaches become more frequent.  
• Recommend routine eye examination given screen work and photophobia.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected: vitals, neurological exam, detailed medication reconciliation (including oral contraceptive use), allergy verification of non-drug allergens.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient answered “Yeah” then “No” to neck pain/stiffness.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor inaudible filler, no major issues.
